title: Cardio-respiratory system & exercise
examples: What is the difference between resting heart rate and maximum heart rate?
How does aerobic exercise improve my lung capacity?
Can you explain what stroke volume means in simple terms?

explain.say: Today we are looking at how exercise affects your heart and lungs. We will learn about three important measurements. These help us understand your fitness level.

draw.text: Heart Rate, Stroke Volume, VO₂ max

explain.say: First we look at heart rate. This is how many times your heart beats in one minute. When you exercise, your heart beats faster to pump more blood.
Next we discuss stroke volume. This is the amount of blood your heart pumps out with each single beat. More volume means a stronger pump.
The third concept is VO₂ max. This measures the maximum rate of oxygen your body can use during exercise. It is a key measure of aerobic fitness.
Think about running a mile. Your heart rate increases because you need more oxygen. Your stroke volume increases because your heart pumps harder. This raises your VO₂ max.

draw.text: Exercise increases heart rate, stroke volume, and VO₂ max.

explain.say: A real-life example is climbing many flights of stairs. You notice your breathing gets faster and your heart beats much quicker. This shows your cardiorespiratory system working hard.

faq.q: Does my resting heart rate tell me everything about my fitness?
faq.a: No, it is just one measure of your fitness. Exercise also improves your stroke volume and VO₂ max. You might also ask: What else measures fitness? How is resting heart rate calculated? Does a low heart rate mean I am fit?
asks: Is heart rate the only measure?

faq.q: What is the relationship between heart rate and stroke volume?
faq.a: They work together to determine cardiac output. Cardiac output is the total amount of blood pumped per minute. You might also ask: How do these two affect each other? Is cardiac output always constant?
asks: How does heart rate affect blood pumping?
What is the total blood pumped per minute?

faq.q: Is a high VO₂ max always better?
faq.a: A higher VO₂ max generally indicates better cardiorespiratory fitness. However, it depends on your age and fitness level. You might also ask: What is the ideal VO₂ max? How is this value tested?
asks: What is the best VO₂ max number?
How do I test my oxygen uptake?

faq.q: Can I improve my VO₂ max just by resting?
faq.a: No, VO₂ max is best improved through regular aerobic exercise. Consistent activity challenges your cardiovascular system. You might also ask: What kind of exercise helps most? How long must I exercise to see results?
asks: What is the best exercise for oxygen uptake?
How quickly can I improve my fitness?

faq.q: Do I need to track all three metrics to be healthy?
faq.a: While knowing these metrics is useful, focusing on consistent activity is most important. Regular exercise benefits your entire system. You might also ask: Are these measurements permanent? Can I improve them naturally?
asks: What is the main goal of fitness training?

facts: Heart rate is measured in beats per minute.
Stroke volume is the volume of blood pumped per beat.
VO₂ max measures maximum oxygen consumption during exercise.
Aerobic exercise strengthens the heart and lungs.
Increased fitness leads to higher stroke volume.

quiz.say: A runner increases their pace, causing their heart to beat faster and pump more blood per beat. Which factor is primarily increasing?
quiz.why: Increasing pace requires more oxygen, which directly increases the required heart rate.

wrong.1: While stroke volume increases, the immediate, noticeable change when speeding up is the heart rate.
wrong.2: VO₂ max is a measure of capacity, not the immediate rate of change in beats per minute.
wrong.3: Blood pressure is affected, but heart rate is the primary variable reflecting the increased effort.

quiz.say: A person who trains regularly shows a higher stroke volume compared to a sedentary person. This improvement is best attributed to:
quiz.why: Regular aerobic exercise strengthens the heart muscle, allowing it to pump more blood with each beat.

wrong.0: Diet affects overall health, but sustained exercise directly trains the heart muscle.
wrong.1: Resting allows the heart to adapt to lower demands, decreasing stroke volume over time.
wrong.2: While strength training is good, aerobic exercise is key for improving blood volume and stroke volume.

quiz.say: If a person's VO₂ max is measured at 35 milliliters per kilogram per minute, what does this number represent?

options.show: The maximum weight the person can lift
options.say: The maximum weight the person can lift

options.show: The maximum rate of oxygen use
options.say: The maximum rate of oxygen use

options.show: The total blood pumped in one minute
options.say: The total blood pumped in one minute

quiz.why: VO₂ max quantifies the highest amount of oxygen your body can utilize during intense exercise.

wrong.0: This measurement relates to oxygen use, not muscular strength.
wrong.2: That describes cardiac output, which uses both heart rate and stroke volume.
wrong.3: Resting heart rate is measured in beats per minute, not milliliters.
